summary: Backend Launch Manager PASSED (20/20 pytest tests including URL validation, is_live logic, anti-premature-click safeguard, admin_log dual-write, and readiness observation across all 4 tones with plural/singular grammar checks). Frontend ribbon renders correctly above BrandMasthead when enabled+future — butterfly icon, 'FriendPlace launches in D·H·M', tagline, no dismiss button — and the ticker DOES update (50→49 min after 62s wait, confirmed). Admin /admin/launch page renders all required sections: George's Launch Readiness card with tone-adaptive palette + Ask George pill, countdown preview card, Countdown/Store/Manual-state/Checklist sections, Sydney time display, date+time inputs. Sidebar has 'Launch' entry. CRITICAL BUG FOUND: live-state and disabled-state transitions do NOT propagate to visitor browsers in real time — the client-side refetch `fetch('/api/public/launch-status')` in LaunchCountdownRibbon.tsx uses a RELATIVE URL that returns 404 (Next.js has no such route), so the ribbon is stuck on whatever SSR delivered until the ISR revalidate window elapses AND a fresh SSR request happens. Verified: 65s wait + hard reload with cache-busting query still showed counting ribbon after backend was flipped to is_live=true.

ui_bugs.issue: Line 43: `fetch('/api/public/launch-status', {cache:'no-store'})` uses a RELATIVE URL and hits the Next.js server on :3001 (which returns 404), not the FastAPI backend. Result: client-side refetch never succeeds, so live-state / disabled transitions never propagate on the browser after initial paint. Must use `${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL}/api/public/launch-status` (mirror the SSR fetch in app/page.tsx line 11).
Line 91: Apple logo span is EMPTY (``) — the App Store button in live mode has no icon glyph while the Play Store button uses '▶'. Cosmetic but visible.

integration_issues.issue: Even after 65s (> revalidate:30) with cache-busting URL query, SSR still served the previously-cached counting-state HTML and the client couldn't correct it because the relative /api/public/launch-status fetch 404s. Compound issue: relative client fetch is broken AND SSR ISR + fetch data-cache holds the response.

action_items: Fix LaunchCountdownRibbon.tsx line 43: replace the relative fetch with `${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL || ''}/api/public/launch-status` so the client can actually poll the backend. Consider adding a small polling interval (e.g. every 60s) so live-state flips on visitor screens without a page reload.

Consider tightening the SSR fetch cache (e.g. revalidate: 10) OR remove `next: {revalidate:30}` in app/page.tsx line 11 so admin flips propagate quickly; combined with the fixed client refetch this closes the transition gap.
Optional cosmetic: put the Apple glyph () back in LaunchCountdownRibbon.tsx line 91 so the live-mode App Store button matches the Play Store button visual weight.
critical_code_review_comments: services/launch.py is clean, well-commented, correct URL regex validation, defensive ISO parsing, and defers store-link exposure via `public_status()` — good.
cms_module.py PATCH endpoint correctly wraps ValueError → 400 and dual-writes audit via `_audit.log_admin_action` with action='launch.settings.update' (verified via /api/cms/admin-log).

Anti-premature-click safeguard verified end-to-end: with is_live=false the public endpoint returns empty strings for appstore_url/playstore_url, and the ribbon only renders store buttons when it derives live=true.

Grammar contract holds: with BOTH stores missing → 'the App Store and Google Play links aren\'t set yet ... I\'d add them'. With only one missing → 'isn\'t set yet ... I\'d add it'. All 4 tones (wait/warn/ready/live) produce coherent readable observations.
seed_data_creation: None. Only mutated the singleton settings/launch doc; restored to enabled=true, launch_at=T+45d, launch_complete=false, valid App Store + Google Play URLs, welcome_message default. is_live=false and store URLs hidden in public response — verified.

Only outstanding item is the client-side relative-fetch bug in LaunchCountdownRibbon.tsx — after main agent fixes it, re-run the frontend live/disabled transition tests (patch launch_complete=true then wait ~5s for polling and confirm ribbon flips without a full page reload). Cleanup left settings enabled + far-future + valid URLs.
rca_of_issue: LaunchCountdownRibbon.tsx uses `fetch('/api/public/launch-status', {cache:'no-store'})` — a RELATIVE URL that resolves against the Next.js origin (:3001), which has no /api/public route (returns 404). Consequently the useEffect refetch always fails silently and the client is frozen on whatever the initial SSR payload contained. Combined with `next: {revalidate:30}` on the SSR fetch (app/page.tsx:11), admin changes to launch_complete/enabled/launch_at can lag visitor browsers by minutes. Repro: PATCH launch_complete=true → GET public/launch-status confirms is_live=true → open http://localhost:3001/ in a browser that already had the counting ribbon; the ribbon does NOT swap to the welcome/live state until the SSR data cache is force-invalidated. Fix: replace relative URL with `${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL || ''}/api/public/launch-status`, mirroring app/page.tsx:11; optionally add a setInterval to re-poll every 60s during the counting window.
